candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Epistola ad Marcellinum §28
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum de Interpretatione Psalmorum (Letter to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 27 (1857). The Letter is Athanasius's principal pastoral-spiritual work — a personal letter to Marcellinus (recovering from illness) explaining how to use each Psalm as prayer for specific spiritual circumstances. Hermeneutic anchor for the Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat) Psalter-recitation tradition.
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Marcellinum §28 (c. 350 AD)

'Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions' (LXX 50:3) — Athanasius marks Ps 51 (LXX 50) as the PENITENTIAL-PRAYER PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-confessing-grave-sin. The eleēson me ho theos kata to mega eleos sou (have mercy on me, O God, according-to thy great-mercy) becomes the canonical-confession-formula for the Tewahedo penitential-tradition. Athanasius's pastoral-instruction: pray Ps 51 not as one observing-David-confessing (third-person) but as one's-OWN-confession-in-David's-voice. The Psalter is the Spirit-given prayer-vocabulary the praying-soul inhabits.

candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Marcellinum §28 (c. 350 AD)

'Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions' (LXX 50:3) — Athanasius marks Ps 51 (LXX 50) as the PENITENTIAL-PRAYER PARADIGM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-confessing-grave-sin. The eleēson me ho theos kata to mega eleos sou (have mercy on me, O God, according-to thy great-mercy) becomes the canonical-confession-formula for the Tewahedo penitential-tradition. Athanasius's pastoral-instruction: pray Ps 51 not as one observing-David-confessing (third-person) but as one's-OWN-confession-in-David's-voice. The Psalter is the Spirit-given prayer-vocabulary the praying-soul inhabits.

candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistulae ad Serapionem 1.9 (c. 350 AD)

'Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me' (LXX 50:13 — to Pneuma to Hagion sou mē antanelēs ap' emou) — Athanasius marks Ps 51:11 (LXX 50:13) as the OT ANTI-PNEUMATOMACHIAN ANCHOR — cited in Letters to Serapion 1.9 against Tropici denial of the Spirit's divinity. The Pneuma to Hagion sou (thy-Holy-Spirit, with possessive-divine-pronoun) makes the Spirit the inalienable-divine-property of God; one does-not-pray-to-not-remove a creature from oneself but God's-own-Spirit. David's-prayer thus articulates pneumatological-divinity centuries before the post-Nicene Trinitarian-articulation. Pairs with Ps 139:7 + 143:10 as the canonical-OT-Holy-Spirit prooftext-triplet.
